In his blog comment, Yuval appears to be offering his apology as a way to get Pachter to take down the blog post. Pachter’s post seems fine to me; I see no reason he should take it down. But Yuval should post the apology anyway. Now that he’s ready and willing to write the honest apology, he should just do it, unconditional on whatever Pachter decides to do. I think this would be an admirable step forward on Yuval’s part.

Otherwise we’re getting into Russell’s paradox territory.

If someone says “I am willing to write an honest apology,” does that itself constitute an apology? I guess that, on a literal level, you can say you’re willing to write an honest apology but then decide not to do it. But do apologies really work like that? Is it meaningful to offer an IOU for an apology? My instinct is: No, once you’ve offered the IOU, you’ve effectively apologized. Even if haven’t signed on the bottom, you’ve written the letter in your own hand (assuming, again, that it’s Yuval who wrote the comment that was under his name).
